Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Public Registry Disclosure

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 95/2018, de 9 de marzo, por el que se crea el Registro de Titularidades Reales; and Ley 1/2010, de 22 de julio, de Sociedades de Capital, for corporate-registry substance requirements.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

Conditional. The Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must maintain a registered office in Spain corresponding to its real place of administration or principal establishment. A virtual administrative address is acceptable for receiving correspondence and legal notices only if the resin-statue production, hand-painting, warehousing, or fulfillment activity is backed by a physical workshop, warehouse, or logistics contract in Spain. A pure virtual office without commercial substance creates non-compliance risk under Ley 1/2010 and Spanish tax-control principles.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office location, under the coordination of the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad, Mercantiles y de Bienes Muebles de España.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 20-23, 28-30, 32, 40-42, 58-62, 78-83, 210-212, 214-216, 225-232, 246-251, and 253-279; Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and internationalization; Law 18/2022, which permits a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada to be incorporated with minimum capital of EUR 1.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) granted before a Spanish notary and submitted for registration with the applicable Provincial Commercial Registry, together with the company bylaws and beneficial ownership information.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 72 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The statutory minimum capital is EUR 1, fully assumed and paid at incorporation. If capital is below EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve until the combined capital and reserve reach EUR 3,000; on liquidation, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital if company assets are insufficient. No statutory escrow account is required. A bank certificate of deposit may be replaced by the founders' express assumption of joint liability for the accuracy of the contribution under Article 62 of the Companies Act.

Funding & unlock path: Obtain the municipal or competent authority fire-safety acceptance required by the activity filing, applying the Technical Building Code fire provisions and the industrial fire-safety regulation where industrial-premises thresholds apply. Verify structural loads, ventilation, electrical installations, machinery guarding, emergency routes, and storage compatibility through qualified technical certification. Implement Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, chemical-agent controls, safety data sheets, personal protective equipment, exposure assessments, emergency procedures, and mandatory worker training. Secure required certificates for low-voltage installations, fire systems, and any pressure equipment before operation.

Paid-in capital rule: The statutory minimum capital is EUR 1, fully assumed and paid at incorporation. If capital is below EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve until the combined capital and reserve reach EUR 3,000; on liquidation, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital if company assets are insufficient. No statutory escrow account is required. A bank certificate of deposit may be replaced by the founders' express assumption of joint liability for the accuracy of the contribution under Article 62 of the Companies Act.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and ratifies the subscription and full payment of its issued shares by the founding shareholder in accordance with the public deed and bylaws; (2) the registered office is adopted at [full Spanish address], with authority granted to update the address within the same municipality where permitted; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, if applicable, directors are appointed as stated in the deed, each accepting office and undertaking the statutory duties of diligence, loyalty, confidentiality, and conflict disclosure; and (4) the appointed officer is authorized to complete all registry, tax, banking, licensing, and operational formalities.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

The competent industry authority of the relevant autonomous community, together with the municipality's licensing department. Spain has no single nationwide manufacturing licensing board for ordinary resin statue production; industrial registration, machinery, electrical, pressure-equipment, and activity controls are allocated between autonomous communities and municipalities.

Category: Municipal licencia de actividad y apertura, or declaración responsable/comunicación previa de actividad and opening, depending on the municipality and premises risk classification; where applicable, registration in the autonomous-community Industrial Establishment Registry (Registro Integrado Industrial).

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — official portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

Step 1: Obtain Número de Identificación de Extranjero (NIE) for each non-resident director/shareholder. Step 2: Reserve the corporate name at the Registro Mercantil Central (certificación negativa de denominación). Step 3: Execute the SL deed before a Spanish notary and apply to AEAT for the provisional CIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) via Modelo 036/037; the provisional CIF converts to a definitive NIF once registration in the Registro Mercantil is completed. Step 4: File Modelo 036 to enroll in the Spanish tax census (Censo de Empresarios), elect the VAT regime, and register for Impuesto sobre Sociedades. Step 5: Obtain an AEAT digital certificate for online filings. Foreign entities lacking a permanent establishment must appoint a tax representative in Spain.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a separate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades at 25% on worldwide income (15% reduced rate for newly incorporated companies in the first two profitable tax periods; 23% reduced rate may apply to the first EUR 500,000 of small-SL profits). Non-resident dividend distributions are subject to withholding tax, reduced under applicable double tax treaties. — Step 1: Obtain Número de Identificación de Extranjero (NIE) for each non-resident director/shareholder. Step 2: Reserve the corporate name at the Registro Mercantil Central (certificación negativa de denominación). Step 3: Execute the SL deed before a Spanish notary and apply to AEAT for the provisional CIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) via Modelo 036/037; the provisional CIF converts to a definitive NIF once registration in the Registro Mercantil is completed. Step 4: File Modelo 036 to enroll in the Spanish tax census (Censo de Empresarios), elect the VAT regime, and register for Impuesto sobre Sociedades. Step 5: Obtain an AEAT digital certificate for online filings. Foreign entities lacking a permanent establishment must appoint a tax representative in Spain.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a separate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades at 25% on worldwide income (15% reduced rate for newly incorporated companies in the first two profitable tax periods; 23% reduced rate may apply to the first EUR 500,000 of small-SL profits). Non-resident dividend distributions are subject to withholding tax, reduced under applicable double tax treaties.

Available election forms

No check-the-box election exists; SLs are mandatorily entity-level taxed. Available elections and special regimes: (i) consolidated corporate tax regime (régimen de consolidación fiscal) requiring ≥70% direct or indirect ownership; (ii) ETVE holding company regime for foreign dividends and capital gains; (iii) patent box and R&D tax credit elections; (iv) VAT simplified, cash-basis, or cooperative special regimes where the SL qualifies; (v) ATAD hybrid-mismatch disallowance rules under Law 27/2014 article 15 bis.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No VAT registration threshold applies; every entity performing economic activities in Spain must register (Modelo 036/037) before commencing. For the simplified VAT regime, the prior-year supply of goods cap is EUR 250,000, but SL entities generally cannot use this regime.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of resin statues and goods to non-EU third countries qualify for the 0% VAT exemption with credit under Ley 37/1992 article 21.1, provided the goods physically leave EU territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter obtains AEAT validation via REGIMEX/CUSDEC. Services directly related to exported goods and offshore services (article 69 LIVA) are 0% rated when the recipient is established outside the EU; comprehensive documentary evidence must be retained.

  • DUA/Documento Único Administrativo (EU Single Administrative Document export declaration; copy bearing the EORI number and AEAT exit validation)
  • Commercial invoice (factura comercial) stating Incoterms, HS code, quantity, and declared export value
  • Packing list (lista de embalaje/bultos) with container and seal numbers
  • Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR signed transport document evidencing physical exit from EU territory
  • Proof of payment and inward remittance (justificante de cobro) including SWIFT/MT103 or bank certificate
  • Contract or purchase order for offshore services export and delivery confirmation

Large enterprises (turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000) must transmit SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) invoice records to AEAT within 4 calendar days (8 days in July); an SL resin-statue home-kit manufacturer below this threshold files Modelo 303 quarterly and Modelo 390 annually. Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing and software integrity rules apply under Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) and Verifactu (RD 1007/2023), with interoperable e-invoice XML/QR stamp obligations phased in during 2025–2026 by taxpayer size. No real-time fiscal clearance blocking exists, but invoice data must be preserved and reproducible on AEAT audit request.

AEAT strictly audits export disproportionality and documentation; failure to prove EU exit within one month after the 90-day deadline triggers VAT assessment at 21% plus statutory late-payment interest and surcharges. Deliberate false zero-rating constitutes a serious/very serious infringement under Ley 58/2003 articles 184 and 187, with penalties up to 150% of the underpaid VAT and retrospective clawback of the 0% benefit; criminal tax fraud under Código Penal article 305 applies where the amount exceeded EUR 120,000, carrying imprisonment of up to 5 years and director and tax-representative liability.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a euro-area jurisdiction with full currency convertibility under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63-66). Both current-account and capital-account transactions are unrestricted for residents and non-residents; profit remittance and dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders are freely transferable, subject to the domestic 19% non-resident dividend withholding tax, which may be reduced under a double-tax treaty or exempted under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. No prior FX authorization is required for capital inflow or outflow, but all cross-border payments exceeding €12,500 per transaction or €50,000 in annual positions must be reported statistically to the Bank of Spain via BS-1 declarations.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion quota, or statutory repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may freely retain foreign currency receipts in domestic or offshore accounts. The only compulsory obligation is the statistical/financial reporting of balances and transactions under the Bank of Spain's Circular 4/2012 (Declaration of Transactions and Positions), including threshold-based declarations. Non-compliance can trigger administrative fines but does not restrict export flows or profit allocation.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), in coordination with the Directorate General for International Trade and Investments (Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones – DGCIIN) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business for capital-movement oversight

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Stripe Fit: High

Feasibility Rating: Medium. Spanish-licensed or EEA-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) can provide multi-currency IBANs via PSD2 and real-time SEPA/SEPA Instant rails, with optional SWIFT-access partner banks. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot grant credit, must safeguard client funds in tier-one custodial accounts, and must perform full KYC/AML equivalent to banks. For this low-risk resin-statue business, an EMI is viable as a collection gateway for preorder deposits and PayPal/Stripe settlement, but obscurity and counterparty limits mean that the primary treasury ledger should reside with a licensed credit institution. Offshore non-EEA EMIs are not recommended due to lack of depositor protection and potential prohibition on commercial activity without a Spanish branch.

PayPal Fit: High

Feasibility Rating: Medium. Spanish-licensed or EEA-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) can provide multi-currency IBANs via PSD2 and real-time SEPA/SEPA Instant rails, with optional SWIFT-access partner banks. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot grant credit, must safeguard client funds in tier-one custodial accounts, and must perform full KYC/AML equivalent to banks. For this low-risk resin-statue business, an EMI is viable as a collection gateway for preorder deposits and PayPal/Stripe settlement, but obscurity and counterparty limits mean that the primary treasury ledger should reside with a licensed credit institution. Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

High-volume pre-order deposits received via Stripe/PayPal before physical production is documented

Root cause: High-volume pre-order deposits received via Stripe/PayPal before physical production is documented

Defense evidence: Commercial invoice with itemized product SKU, manufacturing timeline, refund policy, Stripe/PayPal payout reports, and customer identity excerpts (pseudonymized where required); purchase orders for resin and packaging materials from suppliers; customs declarations for prior sample shipments.
Invoicing of limited-edition statues at prices above the standard market range for resin collectibles

Root cause: Invoicing of limited-edition statues at prices above the standard market range for resin collectibles

Defense evidence: Independent art-valuation or auction-house comparative appraisal; insurance policy for the collection; certificate of authenticity and edition-numbering registry; escrow agreement or intellectual-property license showing exclusivity premium.
Payments from mixed-source vehicles (PayPal personal accounts, third-party prepaid cards) with subsequent refunds to different instruments

Root cause: Payments from mixed-source vehicles (PayPal personal accounts, third-party prepaid cards) with subsequent refunds to different instruments

Defense evidence: Written refund policy strictly requiring refunds only to the original payment instrument; reconciliation ledger mapping transaction IDs; evidence of goods physical dispatch (tracked courier, customs form CN22/CN23); internal fraud-prevention procedure summary.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

The shareholder subscribes the capital via an incoming SWIFT MT103 from a personal or corporate account, using purpose code 'EQUI' (equity injection) and the Spanish descriptive code 'Aportación de capital social – Constitución SL'. The bank will require a certified copy of the deed of incorporation evidencing the capital subscription and the depositary certificate (certificación bancaria de desembolso) issued by the receiving bank. For amounts above €10,000, the origin of funds must be documented (salary slips, sale agreement, or liquidation certificate of an existing entity), and anti-money-laundering proof may include a sworn statement of lawful origin. The NIF provisional or definitive of the SL must be displayed on the transfer reference.Operational trade settlements for resin materials, packaging, and outsourced sculpture painting are routed through: (a) SWIFT MT103 for non-EU suppliers (China, Vietnam, USA) with purpose code 'Merchandise trade' and supporting invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and inspection certificate; (b) a commercial documentary letter of credit (UCP600) for bulk orders exceeding an agreed threshold to secure both sides; (c) SEPA CT payment for EU-based tooling and workshop costs; (d) PayPal/Stripe payouts to affiliates or refunds, strictly with a Sidebar clearing schedule. Spanish banks may require presentation of the commercial invoice and freight document within 30 days of wire execution for regulatory statistical reporting.Outright FX forwards (EUR/CNY, EUR/USD) executed under a standard documented ISDA Master Agreement or a simplified European Banking Authority-compliant FX Forward contract with a Spanish or EU credit institution.Cross-currency swaps (EUR/CNY, EUR/USD) for medium-term commercial balances, subject to corporate treasury authorization and underlying trade-flow verification.Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY or illiquid emerging-market currencies with a licensed EU bank, permitted solely where an economic exposure exists and cannot be settled in deliverable form.FX options (call/spreads) purchased from a licensed Spanish or EU investment firm for limited downside protection, with no speculative premium beyond 120 days' projected trade exposure.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Spanish-licensed or EEA-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) can provide multi-currency IBANs via PSD2 and real-time SEPA/SEPA Instant rails, with optional SWIFT-access partner banks. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot grant credit, must safeguard client funds in tier-one custodial accounts, and must perform full KYC/AML equivalent to banks. For this low-risk resin-statue business, an EMI is viable as a collection gateway for preorder deposits and PayPal/Stripe settlement, but obscurity and counterparty limits mean that the primary treasury ledger should reside with a licensed credit institution. Offshore non-EEA EMIs are not recommended due to lack of depositor protection and potential prohibition on commercial activity without a Spanish branch.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% (unless reduced under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or applicable tax treaty)

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 days following the six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, deadline is July 25 of the following year).

Deadline: · Frequency:

Due within the first 20 calendar days of April, July, October, and January (for the preceding quarter).

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 Tax identification number (NIF) and corporate details Non-resident entities must provide their foreign tax ID and Spanish permanent establishment (PE) reference if applicable. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due. Surcharges for late payment: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest.
Box 2 Accounting profit (resultado contable) before tax adjustments For non-residents with a PE, report income attributable to the PE only. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due. Surcharges for late payment: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest.
Box 3 Permanent differences (e.g., non-deductible expenses, exempt income) Adjust for items not deductible under Spanish tax law; ensure treaty exemptions are properly claimed. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due. Surcharges for late payment: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest.
Box 4 Temporary differences (e.g., depreciation, provisions) Apply Spanish depreciation rules; for PE, use consistent accounting policies. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due. Surcharges for late payment: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest.
Box 5 Taxable base (base imponible) after offsetting prior-year tax losses Offset losses only if legally available; non-residents may offset losses from the same PE. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due. Surcharges for late payment: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest.
Box 6 Tax rate and gross tax liability Apply standard 25% rate or reduced 15% if eligible; non-residents with PE use same rates. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due. Surcharges for late payment: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest.
Box 7 Deductions, credits, and withholdings Claim treaty relief, double tax credits, and any applicable incentives; attach supporting documentation. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due. Surcharges for late payment: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest.
Box 8 Final tax payable or refund due Ensure all payments are made via the AEAT system; non-residents must use a Spanish bank account or authorized intermediary. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due. Surcharges for late payment: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest.
Box 1 Taxable base for the quarter (based on accounting profit of the year-to-date) Non-residents with PE must compute based on PE income; use the same method as annual return. Late filing penalty of 5% of the amount due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Late payment surcharges as described for Form 200.
Box 2 Applicable percentage (typically 18% for large companies, 17% for others, or 25% if using the alternative method) Non-residents with PE follow the same percentage rules as domestic entities. Late filing penalty of 5% of the amount due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Late payment surcharges as described for Form 200.
Box 3 Amount to be paid (after deducting prior quarterly payments and withholdings) Ensure proper offset of any tax credits or treaty relief. Late filing penalty of 5% of the amount due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Late payment surcharges as described for Form 200.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File required if net turnover exceeds €10 million; Master File required if the group's consolidated turnover exceeds €50 million. Additionally, Form 232 (Información de operaciones vinculadas) must be filed if related-party transactions exceed €250,000 per counterparty or €1 million in total.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime like the UAE, but applies general anti-abuse rules (GAAR) and the doctrine of 'substance over form'. For holding companies, the Spanish tax authorities may challenge structures lacking commercial substance, and the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) provisions on controlled foreign companies (CFC) and interest limitation rules apply. A Spanish SL must demonstrate real economic activity (e.g., employees, premises, decision-making) to benefit from treaty relief and avoid being classified as a shell company.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax evaded, plus late interest. Criminal prosecution for tax fraud exceeding €120,000 may result in imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount.

Director personal liability: Directors may be held personally liable for tax debts if they fail to exercise due diligence, and may face criminal charges, travel bans, and seizure of personal assets.
Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance

Statutory sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of additional tax (up to 25% of the recharacterized income). Administrative penalties up to €10,000 for non-compliance with substance documentation.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly liable for the company's tax liabilities if they knowingly participated in the sham arrangement, and may face disqualification from serving as directors.
AML (Anti-Money Laundering) Violations

Statutory sanction: Fines up to €150,000 for serious infractions, and up to €1.5 million for very serious infractions. Criminal liability for money laundering can lead to imprisonment from 6 months to 6 years.

Director personal liability: Directors can be held criminally liable if they knowingly participate in or fail to prevent money laundering, leading to imprisonment, fines, and travel bans.
Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance

Statutory sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 15% of the adjusted amount (or 25% if the adjustment exceeds €1 million), plus late interest. Failure to file Form 232 incurs a penalty of €1,000 per data item, with a minimum of €10,000.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant transfer pricing policies, and may face disqualification from managing companies.
